svg.title: Expected subalgebras, factor fibres, and hypercentral equality
svg.desc: Each element of the bicentralizer belongs to an expected separable algebra equal to its own bicentralizer. Almost every factor fibre has scalar centralizer and is equal to its own bicentralizer. The separable type III one bicentralizer theorem excludes nonscalar fibres. The resulting centralizer inclusion gives the hypercentral equality using HUC.

g.text: From one element to separable factor fibres
N has a faithful normal state θ. No separability assumption on N.
B has a θ-preserving expectation, and B(B, θ|B) = B. §02
a ∈ C ⊆ B, generated by the rational modular orbit of a
C has separable predual and a state-preserving expectation. §03
χ = θ|C; B(C, χ) = C, hence Cχ = Z(C). §02
Central decomposition into separable factor fibres Cₜ
(Cₜ)χₜ = ℂ1 and B(Cₜ, χₜ) = Cₜ almost everywhere. §§04–06
Measurable witnesses: state error ≤ 1/k; squared commutator ≥ ε²ν(E).
A nonscalar fibre would be type III₁
The earlier factor theorem would then give B(Cₜ, χₜ) = ℂ1.
Together with B(Cₜ, χₜ) = Cₜ, this forces Cₜ = ℂ1.
Therefore C is abelian, and modular restriction gives a ∈ Nθ. §07
Centralizer membership plus commutation with constant centralizer tests.
For separable-predual M: A = M′ ∩ Mω, ψ = φω|A, F = Mω.
HUC gives Aψ = F and F′ ∩ A = B(A, ψ), hence F′ ∩ A = Z(F).
